item: roblox/src/server/ShadowLedger.luau:41-50 does per-entry GetAsync+SetAsync read-modify-write: a lost-update race under concurrency plus write amplification (rewrites the whole entry on each visit). Read the module + its callers, spec the minimal fix (UpdateAsync for atomic read-modify-write; batch if the caller loop rewrites N entries per visit), implement, receipt comment citing t63. Keep the DataStore schema unchanged (existing saved entries must stay readable).
note: Race fixed, no batch, no schema change. Spec landed first in roblox/README.md (durable write law added to the ShadowLedger bullet BEFORE the code: one UpdateAsync per append, appends serialize across servers, value stays a plain array of entry rows). Code: ShadowLedger.luau record() :58-67 now does pcall(store:UpdateAsync(key, transform)) replacing the :43-50 GetAsync+SetAsync pair; transform copies old rows to a fresh table then appends, side-effect free and non-yielding, because the official docs (GlobalDataStore.md, fetched 2026-09-25) say the transform 'will be called as many times as needed' with prior results discarded and 'cannot yield', so a mutating transform could double-append on retry. Batch REJECTED per the item's own condition: caller census shows every ShadowLedger.record call site files ONE event; the sole record() in a loop (SteerFieldZone.luau:103) iterates different players with a break, so no same-key N-per-visit loop exists, and buffering rows would trade durability for size. Receipt comment :43-57 cites t63.next_steal plus the doc quotes.

If event volume ever matters, gopher t75 adds a per player-day coalescing queue (short window, BindToClose + PlayerRemoving flush) and must price the durability tradeoff in the spec first; current volumes do not justify it.
